openings.claim: Needs-based reassignment may resolve exclusion caused by inherited allocations and missing compatibility information.
openings.discriminator: Compare schedules against identical recorded demand: improvement supports allocation mismatch; incompatible evening or piano demand can leave aggregate slack unusable.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4: existing rooms, hours, equipment, no fees, offline requests, performance locks and requested weekly 60-minute guarantees; agree changes with groups.
openings.probe: Ask contacts by phone or in person for total weekly duration, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable session length. Build an eight-week paper schedule, protecting performances and weekly guarantees before allocating additional time. Compare with incumbent fulfillment; 60 minutes does not fully meet a longer need.
openings.uncertainty: Reliable contact reports and feasible allocation remain unproven; blank equipment fields imply no flexibility, and 90% fulfillment currently lacks a denominator.

openings.claim: An authoritative ledger with explicit confirmation may reduce record divergence, misunderstood changes and reconciliation work.
openings.discriminator: Fewer divergent copies supports record consistency; conflicts despite matching current confirmations suggest communication, interpretation or another cause. Added recording overhead may outweigh savings.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4, including offline verbal confirmation, guarantees and performances; staffing feasibility unproven.
openings.probe: Pilot numbered reservations and changes with explicit supersession; update the authoritative desk record before room/date/time readback, mark online updates and timestamps. Track confirmation IDs, conflict circumstances, needs fulfillment and all administration over eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Volunteer/desk adherence is assumed; record inconsistency explains only some conflicts.
